layout: rows = tahsils within districts/states; columns = mother tongue x subsidiary language, Males/Females
footnotes: *In the case of these tahsils the figures in columns 7 and 8 are approximate; all other figures are actuals. (printed at foot of p. 491; asterisked tahsils carry "starred": true)
notes: Table XV Part II 'Bi-lingualism', one opening pp. 490-491 (continued from leaf 504 to 505; header printed only on p. 490). Only Males and Females are printed (no Persons column): persons is null throughout. Rows = tahsils grouped under district (area_path = [United Provinces, district]); only tahsils where bilingualism was recorded are listed. Columns: 3-4 total returning mother tongue Bhotia, 5-6 of whom subsidiary Hindustani; 7-8 total returning mother tongue Hindustani; 9-24 of whom subsidiary Bhotia, Marathi, Oriya, Bihari, Rajasthani, Haburi, Punjabi, Nepali; 25-28 Haburi total / subsidiary Hindustani; 29-32 Kanjari; 33-36 Kanphari; 37-40 Nati. Records with subsidiary null are the 'total who returned mother-tongue X' columns (not a subsidiary language). null in males/females = printed '..' (nil); a record is emitted when at least one of the pair is printed. Page is printed sideways (rotated 90 deg clockwise to read) and slightly skewed: small figures in the right-hand columns sit up to ~20 px (about 2/3 of a row) lower than the row's figures in cols 7-8, so row placement was fixed by measuring baselines and counting row-dot clusters (work/blobs.py) rather than by eye alone. No totals are printed in this table (no district/province total rows), so the only arithmetic checks are subsidiary <= total for each mother tongue (all pass). 62 tahsil rows, Cawnpore to Benares State; continues from leaf 504. District 'Fatehpur' partly broken in print ('F.tehpur'). Mohammadabad (Ghazipur) col 21 figure printed with a damaged glyph resembling 'J'; read as 1. Cross-check: Tehri-Garhwal 'Whole State' cols 7-8 (173,282 / 176,232) equal the Hindustani males/females for Tehri-Garhwal in Part I (leaf 498).
